The circles $r=2$ and $r=2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates of the point $B?$
question.worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ r=2\end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solving for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =2 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},\text{ }\,{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}={45}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}={135}^{∘}.$ 

Also, notice that $r=2$ at both intersection points.

Therefore, polar coordinates of the point $B$ are 

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(2,{135}^{∘}).$
